newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's PRI holds three states - final results.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's PRI holds three states - final results.

text.p: Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has held on to three of the six state governorships up for election, despite allegations of fraud, final results showed on Friday.

The official results showed the PRI retaining the tiny state of Colima, the central state of San Luis Potosi and the southeastern state of Campeche on the Yucatan peninsula in Sunday's mid-term elections.

But preliminary results suggest the PRI lost Mexico's industrial heartland of Nuevo Leon and the state of Queretaro to the conservative National Action Party (PAN), which already controls four of the country's 32 states.
The PRI was likely to hold off a PAN challenge in Sonora, on the northern border with the United States. Final official scores in these three states were due by Sunday.

The PRI was trounced in the race for Mexico City mayor and lost its absolute majority in the lower house of Congress for the first time in seven decades in the watershed elections that changed the balance of power away from one-party rule.

The final tally for Campeche showed PRI candidate Antonio Gonzalez Curi winning 48.01 percent of the vote against Layda Sandores, candidate of the left-wing opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), with 41.2 percent.

Earlier this week the PRD burned ballot papers in protest at alleged foul play at some 200 polling centres in Sunday's state elections. Sansores led 12,000 people through the streets of Campeche city to drive the message home.
Mexico's two largest political parties, the PRD and the PAN, joined forces to file formal charges of fraud against the ruling PRI even before final results were tallied.
In San Luis Potosi final offical results in the governor's race gave PRI candidate Fernando Silva Nieto 45.5 percent of votes over PAN's Marcelo de los Santos who won 38.1 percent.
The PRI's candidate for Colima, Fernando Moreno, won the state governorship there with 41.4 percent of the vote over the PAN's Enrique Michel, who obtained 37.2 percent.
